clue.text: Tricky sums are set for a scholar

indicators.note: tricky sums are awkward ones, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Difficult arithmetic problems are being set to test a learned person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky' rearranges SUMS ARE; 'set for' just joins. Erasmus was the Dutch Renaissance humanist.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus of Rotterdam was the great Renaissance humanist and classical scholar.

clue.text: See it as possibly the simplest solution

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Advice to treat this as the most straightforward answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SEE IT AS; 'solution' is a nod to the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: The least difficult option is the least complicated one.

clue.text: Non-professional from a dull back street in Paris

parts.note: matt (or mat) describes a dull, unpolished finish

indicators.note: back says the French word for street is read backwards

parts.note: rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A hobbyist found in a drab Parisian side street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back street' looks like an alley, but 'back' turns RUE, the French street, into EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does something for love rather than pay is unpaid, a hobbyist.

clue.text: Appearing surprisingly trim in ski clothing

indicators.note: surprisingly hints the letters land in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Someone looking unexpectedly slim in skiwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges TRIM IN SKI.
explanation.definitionFit: A very short skirt is a garment, a piece of women's clothing.

clue.text: Hastily prepared score

explanation.surface: A rough tally knocked together quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Hastily prepared: a scratch team is assembled at short notice; score: to scratch is to mark a surface with a line.

clue.text: A competitor not doing well in either finals or annual exams

indicators.note: the answer sits in the run of letters inside the words finals or annual

explanation.surface: A student who failed both their final and yearly exams.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to a run across the words: finALS OR ANnual. An 'also-ran' is a horse or competitor that finishes out of the places.
explanation.definitionFit: An also-ran is a loser in a race or contest, someone who took part but was unplaced.

clue.text: Offers evidence at trials

parts.note: tests are trials

explanation.surface: A witness gives testimony during court hearings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trials' suggests court, but means experiments.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear witness formally is to vouch for or certify something.

clue.text: A military music man — and very superior with it!

parts.note: so means very
U means upper-class or superior
SA, sex appeal, is crossword's 'it'

explanation.surface: A grand army bandmaster who is rather pleased with himself.
explanation.walkthrough: John Philip Sousa was the American 'March King'; U is the British label for upper-class, and 'it' as SA means sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: John Philip Sousa wrote famous marches such as The Stars and Stripes Forever for US bands.

clue.text: There's some purpose in ripped clothing

indicators.note: the word for purpose goes inside the word for ripped

parts.note: rent is the past of rend, meaning torn
an aim is a purpose

explanation.surface: Torn garments still have some use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ripped' reads as describing the clothing, but it is a piece of wordplay; 'some' is filler and the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is a literary word for garments.

clue.text: Sort of thing that is assumed when retiring

definitions.text: Sort of thing that is assumed when retiring

parts.words: Sort of thing that is assumed when retiring
parts.note: retiring means going to bed, and assumed means put on, so a garment worn in bed

explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests leaving work; here it means going to bed, and 'assumed' means put on.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose dress worn for sleeping is put on at bedtime.

clue.text: Composer with a colourful career?

explanation.surface: A musician whose life was full of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir John Stainer was an English Victorian church composer; read literally, a stainer is one who applies colour for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Composer: Sir John Stainer wrote The Crucifixion; a colourful career: a person who dyes or tints things works with colour.

clue.text: Courting custom

parts.note: reads like an old tradition of romance, but means actively seeking customers or trade

explanation.walkthrough: 'Custom' here means business from customers, not a tradition, and 'courting' means soliciting it.
explanation.definitionFit: Touts pester passers-by to buy, so soliciting trade aggressively is what they do.

clue.text: Odds, oddly enough

parts.note: a betting price whose name is the opposite of odd, which is the oddity the clue enjoys

explanation.walkthrough: In betting, a price of one to one is called by a name meaning the opposite of 'odd', hence 'oddly enough'.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-to-one betting price is a set of odds whose name is the reverse of odd numbers.

clue.text: Will meant to go straight following investigation

indicators.note: the reworked letters come after the word for investigation

parts.note: a test is an examination or investigation

indicators.note: going straight means reforming, so the letters of meant are reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone intended to give up crime after a police inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go straight' means to reform, the wit of the anagram signal; 'Will' looks like a verb but is the legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A last testament is the legal document by which a person leaves their property, the same as a will.

clue.text: Film seen by a sailor mid-evening is hot!

parts.note: a tar is a crossword sailor

indicators.note: mid-evening asks for the central letter of the word evening

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Excited remark that a seaman watching a film in the evening finds it very hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, but it means a dull coating; 'mid' takes N, the central letter of EVENING.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull layer that forms on metal exposed to air is a discoloured coating, a thin skin over silver.

clue.text: Article occupying people in Washington

indicators.note: the article takes up a place inside the word for people

parts.note: to settle a land is to people or populate it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A news item about who lives in America's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occupying' puts A inside SETTLE. 'Washington' means the US state, not the capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Seattle is the largest city of Washington State in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Standing by for a lengthy party

parts.note: long means lengthy
a side is a party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: Waiting around for a gathering that goes on for hours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a celebration but means a faction.
explanation.definitionFit: To be next to someone, at their side, is to stand by them.

clue.text: Germ-free space — it may get polluted

indicators.note: polluted letters are spoilt and jumbled, so space and it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sterile area is at risk of contamination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may get polluted' rearranges SPACE and IT together.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile surgical conditions are free of bacteria and infection.

clue.text: A game cut short

parts.note: bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A match brought to an early end.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense a book by trimming text is to shorten it.

clue.text: Call up a goddess in spring

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for call is read bottom to top

parts.note: to name is to call
Ate is the Greek goddess of folly and ruin

explanation.surface: Summon a goddess during the spring season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call up' looks like summon, but 'up' reverses NAME to EMAN; 'spring' is the verb, as in issue forth.
explanation.definitionFit: To issue or flow out from a source is to arise from it.

clue.text: Talk about a mad fellow

parts.note: c, circa, means about
the Mad Hatter of Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: A conversation about an unhinged man.
explanation.walkthrough: C is circa, Latin for about; the Hatter in Alice's Adventures in Wonderland is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle talk is rapid, trivial conversation.

clue.text: He can be relied upon to play his part

definitions.text: He can be relied upon to play his part

parts.words: He can be relied upon to play his part
parts.note: describes a dependable team member, and literally an actor in a touring company who takes a role

explanation.walkthrough: The everyday sense is a reliable, uncomplaining person; the literal sense is a member of a theatrical company.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart who always does their bit is called this, as is a seasoned stage performer.

clue.text: Rushed around American quarter to obtain some silk

indicators.note: the word for rushed wraps the other pieces

parts.note: tore means rushed
US is American
S, south, is a quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone hurried round a US neighbourhood to buy silk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rushed' looks like the start of a scene, but it supplies the outer piece; 'quarter' is a compass point. Tussore comes from wild Indian silkworms.
explanation.definitionFit: Tussore is a coarse silk produced by Indian wild silkworms.

clue.text: The company's overmuch absorbed in design

indicators.note: the word for overmuch is taken inside the word for design

parts.note: a plan is a design
too means excessively

explanation.surface: A firm is too wrapped up in its own scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link; a platoon is properly smaller than a company, but crossword usage allows any military unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A platoon is a unit of soldiers, a military company.

clue.text: Placing naval officers in unimagined situation

indicators.note: the officers go inside the word for unimagined

parts.note: real things are actual, not imagined
POs are petty officers

explanation.surface: Putting sailors into an imaginary scenario.
explanation.walkthrough: 'situation' only completes the surface; POs are petty officers in the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposal is the act of setting or reposing something, a placing.

clue.text: Comes, not for the first time, to gather fruit

definitions.text: Comes, not for the first time

parts.note: to reap is to gather a harvest
pears are a fruit

explanation.surface: Someone returns again and again to pick the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up again after an absence is to come back once more.

clue.text: The little page working late gets double

parts.note: p is the short form of page

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into another order

explanation.surface: A page boy who works late is paid twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges LATE; 'double' is a fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A fold in fabric doubles the material over on itself.

clue.text: A note to file — "hold on"

parts.note: G is a musical note
a rasp is a coarse file

explanation.surface: A memo pinned on the board telling someone to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold on' reads as 'wait', but 'hold' is the definition and 'on' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To grip something firmly in the hand is to take a firm hold of it.

clue.text: Varying geographically, in a manner of speaking

definitions.text: Varying geographically, in a manner of speaking

parts.words: Varying geographically, in a manner of speaking
parts.note: a way of talking that changes from region to region; 'in a manner of speaking' looks like a hedge but is literal

explanation.walkthrough: 'in a manner of speaking' usually means 'so to speak'; here it literally describes a form of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A regional variety of a language, with its own words and accent, differs by area.

clue.text: An order one with intelligence finds sinister

parts.note: OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
I is the Roman numeral for one
nous is common sense or intelligence

explanation.surface: A clever honoured person discovers something wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: OM is the Order of Merit, an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Something threatening or foreboding seems to promise harm.

clue.text: Old German prince, a choosy individual

explanation.surface: A historic German aristocrat who was fussy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Holy Roman Emperor was chosen by German princes holding this title.
explanation.definitionFit: Old German prince: one of the rulers who chose the Holy Roman Emperor; a choosy individual: a voter, someone who chooses.

clue.text: Long-lived oriental bird — a pound only

parts.note: E stands for east, the oriental direction
a tern is a seabird
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An Asian bird that lives a long time costs only a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting goes on without end, far beyond merely lasting long.
